name: bento4
desc: Full-featured MP4 format and MPEG DASH library and tools
why: Its mp4dump tool exposes the box structure inside MP4 and DASH files, a useful way to take media files apart.

brief.what_it_is: Bento4 is a C++ class library and command-line toolkit for reading and writing ISO-MP4 files, plus packaging for MPEG DASH, HLS and CMAF. It takes in MP4 files and elementary streams (H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, AAC) and produces things like fragmented MP4, encrypted or decrypted MP4, MPEG-TS, HLS playlists and segments, DASH presentations, and metadata edits. It ships about thirty command-line tools, including mp4info for track and codec summaries and mp4dump for the full box tree of a file. The README says the SDK does not depend on any external library.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a fast, modern, open source toolkit for all MP4 and DASH/HLS/CMAF media format needs. It notes that ISO-MP4 is derived from Apple QuickTime, so it also reads and writes most QuickTime files.
brief.how_it_works: The tools are built on the Bento4 C++ SDK API and operate on the ISO-MP4 box (atom) structure, so tools like mp4edit and mp4extract can add, replace, or pull out individual boxes. Packaging tools such as mp4fragment, mp4dash and mp42hls read samples from existing MP4 files and write new segments, playlists and manifests. Encryption tools implement several schemes, including MPEG Common Encryption (CENC), PIFF, ISMA, and OMA DCF. The README does not describe the internal design in more detail.

brief.install_notes: The README covers build paths rather than a brew-style install. Options are Make with Build/Targets/<arch>-<vendor>-<os> files, CMake (Makefiles, Xcode, Visual Studio, or Android NDK with an NDK toolchain file), SCons, Xcode projects for macOS and iOS, a Visual Studio 2010 solution for Windows, or vcpkg. The Android CMake path needs the NDK, an ABI such as arm64-v8a, and a minimum API level. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned. Prebuilt SDKs and tools are on a separate Downloads page that I did not open.
brief.standout: It is a self-contained C++ library with no external dependencies that covers the whole MP4 stack, from box-level inspection to DASH and HLS packaging and multiple DRM-compatible encryption schemes. The inspection tools mp4info and mp4dump let you examine the structure of any MP4 or DASH file from the command line.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The GitHub README has a CI badge and release notes up to 1.6.0-638, which mention new AV1 support and a move to MkDocs docs. No release dates or last commit date were visible in what I fetched, so the timing is unknown.
brief.caveats: The README says SCons support is deprecated. Windows is covered by a VS2010 solution file, which looks dated. The README lists DRM support for Marlin, PlayReady and Widevine, while the homepage also names FairPlay and Adobe Access. Licensing is dual, with details only on an About page I did not read. The homepage has a typo, mp4decryp, where the tool is mp4decrypt. The brew executables list includes mp4hls and mp4dashclone, which the GitHub README table does not mention; the homepage does list them. The homepage promises Dolby Vision and HDR support, which the README does not mention.
quotes: A fast, modern, open source C++ toolkit for all your MP4 and DASH/HLS/CMAF media format needs.
The implementation does not rely on any external library. All the code necessary to compile the SDK and tools is included in the standard distribution.

judge.reason: Bento4 makes MP4’s hidden box structure inspectable and editable, then turns that understanding into a toolkit for packaging and transforming media.

entry.title: Bento4
entry.tldr: A C++ MP4 toolkit whose mp4dump prints the full box tree of any MP4 file, so you can see how video containers are built.
entry.deeper_look:
Bento4 is a C++ class library and about thirty command-line tools for reading and writing ISO-MP4 files. It also packages media for MPEG DASH, HLS and CMAF. Inputs are MP4 files and elementary streams (H.264, H.265, AAC). Outputs include fragmented MP4, MPEG-TS, HLS playlists and segments, DASH presentations, and encrypted or decrypted files.

The door into something larger is the box structure. An MP4 file is a tree of boxes (QuickTime called them atoms), each with a type and a size, nested inside one another. `mp4info` gives a summary of tracks and codecs. `mp4dump` shows the entire box tree. `mp4edit` and `mp4extract` can add, replace or pull out individual boxes. Most of what a player does with a file starts at this level.

The packaging tools show what streaming video does behind the scenes. `mp4fragment` rewrites a file into fragments, and `mp4dash` and `mp42hls` produce manifests and segments from it. The encryption tools implement several schemes, including MPEG Common Encryption (CENC), PIFF, ISMA and OMA DCF. The README says the SDK relies on no external library.
entry.install:
brew install bento4
# the formula depends on python@3.15; no account or hardware needed

try_this.what_happens: Lists the options for the tool that summarizes tracks and codecs in an MP4 file.
Shows how to print the full atom/box structure of an MP4 file.
Shows the options for building a DASH presentation from MP4 input.

entry.whats_unique: It covers the whole MP4 stack in one self-contained library, from box-level inspection to DASH and HLS packaging and several encryption schemes. Most similar tools do only one of those jobs.
entry.caveats: The README marks its SCons build as deprecated, and no release dates were visible, so how recently it has been updated is unclear.
